_: Each design screen and how to reach the same state in the built app (agentic-system ADR-0040, Tech Lead's plan for GH-58). route: where the built app shows a screen of that name today, even an old version of it; null only when no screen of that name is built yet. path: the decided English route (navigation.md). A build issue sets route = path in the diff that ships the screen. A redrawn screen's comparison deliberately shows the old-built screen next to the new design: that mismatch is expected until its build issue lands. Each subtask adds a screen's entry in the diff that creates its .dc.html, or, when the entry compares one block of an existing file (the Estados<State> entries do; the customer form's entries compare NuevaVentaCliente's 'Nuevo cliente' block, because customers.md makes it the same form), in the diff that needs the comparison; only the chrome subtask removes entries, together with the file. {name} placeholders come from the sample app's facts. Steps: click (exact text), press (the exact accessible name of a button, found by role and strict: for an icon-only control that has no text), fill (label + value, which takes {email} and the ids too), wait (text); assertScreens refuses any other shape, and a step with more than one key. tema: 'oscuro' forces the dark theme on the built capture via data-tema, the only value the app recognises (the system's own color scheme never picks it; both captures always run with colorScheme: 'light'). screen is the unique key of an entry: its PNG name, its --only key and its heading; assertScreens refuses a repeat. design (optional) names the file pantallas/<design>.dc.html to compare against, default screen; it must exist. section (optional) is the exact label text of one block inside a design file that draws several states: the design column is cropped to the parent block of the first element whose exact text is the label, and the text must occur in the file exactly once (assertScreens refuses a label that is missing or occurs twice, and the capture counts it in the DOM as well, GH-224). The InicioPrimeraVez* drawings hold four frames; the rows compare three of them, each on its own account (InicioPrimeraVez* on primera_vez, InicioOnboardingEnCurso* on en_curso, InicioOnboardingCompleto* on completo, GH-303), and the Oscuro rows take the light file's block with the '· tema oscuro' label where the drawing has one. The imported frame in these drawings is covered by InicioImportado*, so no row repeats it. Frame 1's stale-catalog notice needs a tested Telegram bot, which the sample cannot reach: it is judged by eye. Order matters: comparisons.mjs captures in file order over one sample app, whose Onboarding is unfinished until a capture finishes it, so a capture that changes the Onboarding's state (OnboardingVariedad, OnboardingListo) comes after every capture that needs it unfinished (the Onboarding steps). The Compu twins of the Onboarding steps name the phone file as their design, since the Onboarding has no computer drawing of its own. Steps also take { offline: true }: once the screen has loaded and settled it first loads every font face the page has not loaded yet, then takes the browser offline, with no reload. An Estados<State> entry may compare one block of an existing .dc.html with that state reached on an existing screen through steps, added in the diff that needs the comparison (EstadosConfirmar opens the delete dialog and never confirms it). Dark twins (EntrarOscuro, ResetOscuro, AnalisisOscuro, AnalisisCompuOscuro, PrecioNuevoOscuro, PrecioNuevoCompuOscuro) name their own drawing: <screen>.dc.html, else <design>Oscuro.dc.html, and assertScreens refuses any other design when one of those files exists. The light design file is used only when no dark drawing exists, and then the twin compares structure only; its dark colors are checked by eye against tokens.css. Reset has no design file of its own: it reuses Invitacion's. EstadosGone has no section because no label in Estados.dc.html draws 'Eso ya no está.': the whole file is the design column. Checked by eye, with the steps written in the PR, because no entry here can reach them: loading, the server-error retry, the transient notices ('Eso ya no está. La lista ya está al día.', 'Venta guardada' with Deshacer) and the empty lists. Main and Componentes are the design system itself, not screens, so they have no entry. registry lists every screen of the front, whether or not it has a design file: each is its path, its kind (the navigation.md kind: root, card or form) and its parent's path (a root has none; computer_parent is the parent on a computer when it differs from the phone's); archived_parent, on a variety's page only, is the parent when the record is archived (VarietyPage's useBackParent override, not the registry in web/src/routes.ts), and a kind or a parent changes here and in web/src/routes.ts in the same diff. A screen with a design file is also in screens, which says only where it is built; a screen with none (a stock entry) is only here. The customer form has no design file of its own and keeps its registry rows; it is also in screens, compared against the 'Nuevo cliente' block of NuevaVentaCliente. Every path of screens and of registry is a front path the server may serve or redirect to (tests/test_static_spa.py), `{name}` read as `{id}`. account (optional) is the name of one of the sample's extra businesses, a key of facts.accounts in the sample.json the sample app wrote: the entry signs in with that business's email and password instead of La Huerta's, and its {email} is that business's; it takes no other {placeholder} (the ids are La Huerta's, assertScreens refuses it) and no signed_out. An account's kind is in facts.account_kinds (the sample writes one, `open`, `ended`, `pre_onboarding`, `imported` or `onboarding`, for every key of facts.accounts; the top-level account_kinds list is the set of those kinds, the one list screens.mjs and sample_app.py both answer to, and a test fails when they differ; comparisons.mjs exits 2 before capturing if it is missing or does not match, assertAccountKinds). An `open` account is a business whose Onboarding is still open, there to reach OnboardingListo, which ends an Onboarding for good (ADR-0036): exactly one entry that reaches it names it (assertScreens refuses a Listo entry with no account), and an open account on any other entry is refused. An `ended` account is a business whose Onboarding the sample ended at seed time: read-only entries (the six Inicio rows) may share it, and no Listo entry names it. A `pre_onboarding` account is a business with no Onboarding row (the first-run checklist; `checklist` has one priced variety, `primera_vez` has nothing priced), an `imported` account is one the real import loaded (the after-import notice), and an `onboarding` account is a business whose Onboarding is open at a fixed point and never ended by the sample (`en_curso`: one step done; `completo`: every step answered): all three are read-only, may be shared, and no Listo entry names them (GH-274, GH-303). comparisons.mjs exits 2 before capturing if two selected entries share an open account, an entry names an account that is not in the kinds, or a Listo entry names a read-only one (assertSelectedAccounts). A re-run against the same running sample needs a fresh sample. needs (optional) is the earlier row whose state this row relies on, a screen name: it must name an earlier screen of this file (assertScreens refuses any other), and a selection that keeps the row but drops the one it needs is refused before any capture (assertSelectedNeeds, comparisons.mjs exits 2). OnboardingVariedad saves an opening-stock entry to Mango, the variety of the sample with no entries ({no_entries}), so it comes after every row whose route uses {no_entries} (the EntradaStockSinEntradas rows). Evidence captures run the whole registry in file order with --strict and no --only, each on a fresh sample (ADR-0042); --only is for ae.mjs, which compares one row at a time. Home's evidence for the GH-272 follow-up are the ten rows after InicioCompuOscuro (InicioMesCompu, InicioHoyCompu960, InicioCompu960, InicioMesCompu960, the three Texto130 twins at 960 px and the three at 1280 px, added once the 960 px set at 130 % showed a figure spilling out of its card): screenshots judged by eye, never compared by ae.mjs; Month reuses the Week section because the Month tab has no drawing of its own. design_viewport (optional, [width, height]) is the design side's viewport only: the drawing's own natural width, read by comparisons.mjs where it builds the design context and the design column of the sheet; the built side is always viewport (default the phone). A row has one only with its measured line (scrollWidth, innerWidth, clip) in docs/evidence/GH-548-design-capture.md, and a drawing edit that moves its width is caught only by the next whole-registry strict run.
